- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.67) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80.0), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 3–5 consecutive days, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often misses mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
